title: English Vocabulary in Use — Pre-intermediate and Intermediate · Units 29–30
description: Road infrastructure, driving directions and accident vocabulary; common public notices, restrictions, instructions and safety warnings.
sourceNotice: Prepared from user-supplied reference pages. Vocabulary targets follow the source topics; example sentences and teaching notes are newly written. Source exercises, extended passages, and illustrations are not reproduced.

audit.languagePolicy: All content is in English except Portuguese translations under pt.

units.title: Unit 29 — On the road
units.source: English Vocabulary in Use — Pre-intermediate and Intermediate (4th Edition); printed pages 64–65 (PDF pages 65–66).
units.bookTitle: English Vocabulary in Use — Pre-intermediate and Intermediate (4th Edition)
units.category: Road vocabulary, route directions and road accidents
learningObjectives: Identify roads, junctions, traffic lights, crossings, road signs and motorway lanes.
Interpret driving restrictions, speed limits and road-layout terminology.
Describe a route using get lost, on the way to, via, wrong turning, end up and follow signs.
Describe an accident using precise road and vehicle-action verbs.
Distinguish damage to things from injury to people and use related noun and verb forms.

items.example: This road leads to the town centre.
items.note: A route used by vehicles; may be in or between towns.

items.example: Turn left after the traffic lights.
items.note: A set of coloured lights controlling road traffic. Often plural.

items.example: Slow down when you approach the road junction.
items.note: A place where roads meet.

items.example: There is a sharp bend in the road ahead.
items.note: A curve in a road. Bend can also be a verb.

items.example: The road bends to the right after the bridge.
items.note: A bend can also describe a road changing direction.

items.pt: faixa de pedestres; travessia para pedestres
items.example: The children waited at the pedestrian crossing.
items.note: A marked place where people can cross the road.

items.example: The bridge crosses a narrow river.
items.note: A structure carrying a road or path over a river or another obstacle.

items.example: The road sign warned drivers about the bend.
items.note: A sign beside the road giving instructions or information.

items.example: A no overtaking sign stands just before the bridge.
items.note: Road-sign wording: drivers must not pass another vehicle.

items.example: Do not overtake another car on this narrow road.
items.note: Pass a moving vehicle travelling in the same direction.

items.example: The speed limit is lower near the school.
items.note: The maximum legal speed on a road.

items.example: We joined the motorway outside Bristol.
items.note: British English for a major high-speed road; compare American English freeway or highway.

items.pt: faixa de rodagem; faixa de trânsito
items.example: Stay in your lane until you need to turn.
items.note: One marked part of a road for a line of vehicles.

items.pt: faixa interna; faixa da esquerda em rodovias britânicas
items.example: The lorry stayed in the inside lane.
items.note: On a UK motorway, the lane nearest the left-hand edge; often the normal driving lane.

items.pt: faixa externa; faixa da direita em rodovias britânicas
items.example: She used the outside lane to pass a slower vehicle.
items.note: On a UK motorway, the lane nearest the central reservation, typically used for overtaking.

items.example: The slower vehicles were using the slow lane.
items.note: An informal label for the inside lane; normal lane use depends on local road rules.

items.pt: faixa de ultrapassagem; faixa de veículos mais rápidos
items.example: He moved into the fast lane to overtake.
items.note: An informal label for a faster-moving motorway lane; it is not permission to exceed the speed limit.

items.example: We got lost in the small streets behind the station.
items.note: Not know where you are; past form: got lost.

items.word: on my way to the airport
items.example: I called my sister on my way to the airport.
items.note: Use on my/your/his way to + destination.

items.example: We took a side road to avoid the traffic.
items.note: A smaller road leading off a main road.

items.example: We drove to Bath via a small village.
items.note: Through or by way of a place on the route.

items.pt: pegar a entrada errada; virar na rua errada
items.example: I took the wrong turning and had to drive back.
items.note: Choose an incorrect road where you could turn.

items.pt: entrada; desvio; lugar onde se vira
items.example: Take the second turning on the left.
items.note: A road or point where you turn left or right.

items.example: We ended up at the wrong entrance.
items.note: Arrive in an unintended or unexpected place or situation; often end up + place or -ing.

items.example: There is a free car park next to the library.
items.note: British English for a designated parking area.

items.pt: perguntar a alguém como chegar a um lugar
items.example: We asked a local woman the way to the museum.
items.note: Ask someone the way to + a destination.

items.pt: indicar a alguém o caminho para a estação
items.example: A local woman directed us to the station.
items.note: Give someone directions to a particular place.

items.pt: seguir as placas para o aeroporto
items.example: Follow signs for the airport after the roundabout.
items.note: Use follow signs for + destination.

items.example: There was an accident near the bridge this morning.
items.note: An unexpected event that causes damage or injury.

items.example: The main road was closed for an hour.
items.note: An important road connecting places.

items.example: Drivers must stop when pedestrians are crossing.
items.note: A person travelling on foot.

items.example: Keep your bicycle off the pavement here.
items.note: British English: the path beside the road for people walking; American English sidewalk.

items.pt: sair da calçada; pisar na via
items.example: The boy stepped off the pavement without looking.
items.note: Step off + a raised area and onto the road.

items.example: A lorry was approaching the crossing.
items.note: Move nearer to a place, person or object.

items.example: The driver braked when the light turned red.
items.note: The action of using a vehicle brake to slow or stop.

items.example: Press the brake gently on a wet road.
items.note: The device used to slow or stop a vehicle.

items.pt: desviar bruscamente; mudar de direção de repente
items.example: The car swerved to avoid a fallen branch.
items.note: Change direction suddenly, often to avoid something.

items.example: The van crashed into a wall.
items.note: Crash into + object or vehicle means hit it violently.

items.example: A parked car blocked the entrance.
items.note: A vehicle left in a parking position.

items.pt: lado oposto da via; outro lado da estrada
items.example: The bus stop is on the opposite side of the road.
items.note: Opposite means across from something.

items.example: The fall injured his shoulder.
items.note: Hurt a person or animal, not normally an object.

items.example: No one was injured in the accident.
items.note: Past participle or adjective describing a hurt person.

items.example: The cyclist escaped with a minor injury.
items.note: A physical wound or harm to a person; countable: an injury.

items.example: Both passengers suffered only minor injuries.
items.note: Minor means not very serious.

items.example: The collision damaged the front of the car.
items.note: Harm a thing or property; compare injure for a person.

items.example: The storm caused serious damage to the bridge.
items.note: Normally uncountable in this sense: damage to something.

items.example: The damaged car had to be moved from the road.
items.note: Describes a thing harmed or broken.

items.example: Take the third exit at the roundabout.
items.note: A circular road junction used to control traffic.

items.example: The driver lost control of the car on the wet road.
items.note: Use lose control of + vehicle or situation; past tense lost.

items.example: She braked suddenly to avoid a car in front.
items.note: Avoid + noun can mean act to prevent a collision with something in your path.

sectionsChecked: A: Roads; labelled diagrams of junction, traffic lights, crossing, bends, bridge, road signs and motorway lanes
B: Finding your way; route narrative and numbered explanations
C: An accident; illustrated incident, vocabulary notes and language-help contrast
Exercises 29.1–29.5; answer key on PDF page 220; pronunciation index

units.title: Unit 30 — Notices and warnings
units.source: English Vocabulary in Use — Pre-intermediate and Intermediate (4th Edition); printed pages 66–67 (PDF pages 67–68).
units.bookTitle: English Vocabulary in Use — Pre-intermediate and Intermediate (4th Edition)
units.category: Public signs, prohibitions, instructions and warnings
learningObjectives: Understand common public notices about availability, admission and equipment.
Recognise polite instructions and prohibitions on signs in public places.
Distinguish no entry, no exit and no parking and interpret their practical meaning.
Explain warnings about steps, low ceilings, unattended luggage and fragile parcels.
Identify where typical notices appear without learning entire exercise instructions as lexical targets.

items.example: The notice explains why the lift is closed.
items.note: A displayed message giving information or instructions.

items.example: The ticket machine is out of order.
items.note: Used on machines or equipment that are not working.

items.example: I bought a drink from the vending machine.
items.note: A machine that sells drinks, snacks or other small products.

items.example: The hotel put up a no vacancies sign.
items.note: Hotel notice meaning there are no rooms available.

items.example: The concert is sold out, so we cannot get tickets.
items.note: Nothing remains available for sale; often used for tickets.

items.example: The museum offers free admission on Sundays.
items.note: A notice meaning there is no charge to enter; admission free is also possible.

items.example: Admission to the exhibition is free on Sundays.
items.note: The right or cost of entering a venue.

items.pt: por favor, forme fila do outro lado
items.example: The sign says “Please queue other side”, so we must join the line over there.
items.note: Public instruction: form a line on the other side of the sign.

items.example: Please queue behind the yellow line.
items.note: British English verb meaning wait in an orderly line.

items.example: Keep right as you go down the stairs.
items.note: Instruction to stay on the right-hand side.

items.example: A keep off the grass sign stands beside the lawn.
items.note: Sign prohibiting people from walking on the grass.

items.example: A silence sign was displayed outside the exam room.
items.note: A short instruction to make no noise; displayed with examination in progress.

items.example: The corridor was quiet because an examination was in progress.
items.note: Notice meaning an exam is happening now.

items.example: A no parking sign is fixed to the gate.
items.note: Drivers may not leave their vehicles here.

items.example: The red no entry sign faces drivers at the junction.
items.note: You must not go into the area from this direction; distinct from no exit.

items.example: We tried that corridor, but the sign said no exit.
items.note: You cannot leave through this doorway or route; distinct from no entry.

items.pt: por favor, não perturbe; não incomode
items.example: She left a please do not disturb notice on her hotel door.
items.note: A polite request not to interrupt or enter, often in a hotel.

items.example: Please do not disturb her while she is working.
items.note: Interrupt or bother a person.

items.pt: não deixe bolsas ou malas desacompanhadas
items.example: The station notice tells passengers not to leave bags unattended.
items.note: Security warning: keep your belongings with you.

items.example: An unattended suitcase was reported to security.
items.note: Without anyone watching or looking after it.

items.word: do not lean out of the window
items.pt: não se incline para fora da janela
items.ipa: /duː nɒt liːn aʊt əv ðə ˈwɪndəʊ/
items.example: The train has a notice warning passengers not to lean out of the window.
items.note: Instruction to keep your body inside the vehicle.

items.example: Never lean out of an open train window.
items.note: Bend your body outward through an opening.

items.word: please do not feed the animals
items.pt: por favor, não alimente os animais
items.example: A sign at the zoo says please do not feed the animals.
items.note: Instruction not to give food to animals, often displayed in zoos.

items.example: Read the warning before entering the room.
items.note: A message about possible danger.

items.example: The doorway is low, so mind your head.
items.note: Warning that your head might hit something overhead.

items.example: Mind the step when you enter the shop.
items.note: Warning about a step that may cause someone to trip.

items.example: The box is labelled fragile because it contains glass.
items.note: A warning on packages containing things that break easily.

items.example: The parcel arrived safely this morning.
items.note: An item wrapped or boxed for delivery.

items.example: Take care on the steep stairs.
items.note: A general instruction to be careful.

items.example: Keep left as you enter the station.
items.note: A variant instruction to stay on the left side.

items.pt: rua sem saída para veículos; sem passagem
items.example: The sign said “No through road”, so we turned back.
items.note: A road with no route through to another road for vehicles.

items.example: At the entrance to the bridge, a sign tells cyclists to dismount.
items.note: Instruction for cyclists to get off their bicycles.

items.example: We saw a flat to let notice in the window.
items.note: British English property notice advertising a flat available to rent.

items.example: The entrance to the museum is on the right.
items.note: A place where people go into a building; unlike exit.

B: Do this!; illustrated signs for queuing, direction, grass and examinations
C: Don’t do this!; illustrated prohibitions in public places, hotels, transport and zoos
D: Warnings; illustrated low-door, step and parcel warning signs
Exercises 30.1–30.5; answer key on PDF pages 220–221; pronunciation index
